newsitem.title: CHINA: China in call to fight drought, save harvests.
newsitem.headline: China in call to fight drought, save harvests.

text.p: China has issued a battle cry to fight a worsening drought that is threatening to destroy crops and dash Beijing's hopes of another record harvest, state media said on Sunday.
Since mid-April, drought has struck large areas across northern China, including main grain growing regions in the northeast, and southwestern Sichuan province, the official People's Daily said.
"The drought, which is worsening, will do harm to the late growth of summer crops and spring ploughing right now," the Xinhua news agency said.
The State Council, or cabinet, had issued a notice calling on local authorities to take action to prevent the dry spell from ruining crops, the People's Daily said.
"Governments at all levels and departments concerned should should take prompt actions to combat drought in order to ensure successful spring sowing and a bumper summer harvest," the notice said.
Authorities should irrigate larger areas, urge residents to tighten their use of water and promote water-saving technology in order to ensure a good harvest, the People's Daily said.
The China Meteorological Administration said last month that drought in north China was having an unfavourable influence on spring sowing and the growth of seedlings.
China reaped a bumper grain harvest of 490 million tonnes in 1996, surpassing the previous year's record 466 million tonnes, official figures show.
Last year's record harvest was achieved despite a five-month drought in north-central China and flood damage in southern rice-growing regions.
